title: Power BI Refresh Failed
problem: A Power BI dataset or report refresh does not complete successfully.
symptoms: Refresh history shows Failed.
Visuals may continue showing older data.
The failure can appear only in Power BI Service even when Desktop refresh works.
quickFix: Open refresh history and inspect the exact failure message.
Validate source credentials.
Check gateway status if an on-premises source is involved.
Test the query against the current source schema.
detailedFix: Confirm the data source is reachable from the environment performing the refresh.
Re-authenticate the source using the approved organizational method.
Review gateway mapping and service status.
Open the report in Desktop and refresh locally to isolate query problems.
Republish only after validating the corrected model.
diagnostics: Compare the last successful refresh with the first failed run.
Check whether the failure affects one source or the whole model.
Review gateway logs when permitted by the administrator.
prevention: Document source ownership, credential rotation procedures, gateway dependencies, and refresh schedules.

title: Power BI Gateway Unavailable
problem: Power BI Service cannot reach a configured on-premises data gateway.
symptoms: Refresh fails with gateway-related messaging.
The gateway may appear offline or unavailable.
Other datasets using the same gateway can also fail.
quickFix: Check gateway status in the Power BI Service.
Verify the gateway host is online.
Confirm the gateway service is running.
Check recent network or policy changes.
detailedFix: Verify the gateway cluster members and service health.
Review network connectivity from the gateway host.
Confirm data source mappings and credentials.
Update the gateway according to the organization's change process.
diagnostics: Check whether multiple datasets are affected.
Review gateway event logs with administrator access.
Compare the outage time with infrastructure changes.
prevention: Monitor gateway health and maintain documented ownership and update procedures.

title: Salesforce Login Problem
problem: A user cannot sign in to Salesforce.
symptoms: Login is rejected.
MFA or identity provider prompts may fail.
The issue may affect one user or a wider group.
quickFix: Verify the username and approved sign-in method.
Check the organization's identity provider status.
Confirm MFA is working.
Try the approved alternate login path if available.
detailedFix: Determine whether other users are affected.
Check login history when administrator access is available.
Review profile, permission set, IP range, and login-hour restrictions.
Escalate identity-provider issues to the appropriate administrator.
diagnostics: Capture the exact error text without sharing passwords or tokens.
Check whether the problem is browser-specific.
Review recent identity or security-policy changes.
prevention: Maintain documented identity-provider ownership and recovery procedures.

title: Salesforce API Authentication Failure
problem: An integration cannot authenticate to Salesforce.
symptoms: API requests return authentication errors.
Tokens may be rejected or expired.
The problem may begin after a security-policy change.
quickFix: Verify the environment and endpoint.
Check the integration's authentication configuration without exposing secrets.
Review connected-app and user permissions.
Rotate credentials through the approved secret-management process.
detailedFix: Confirm the integration is using the correct OAuth flow.
Validate connected-app policies.
Check user permissions and session/security restrictions.
Review integration logs for status codes and request IDs.
diagnostics: Compare a known-good request with the failing request.
Check whether failures started after a configuration deployment.
Inspect only non-sensitive log fields.
prevention: Use managed secrets, least privilege, documented token rotation, and monitoring.

title: Jira Automation Is Not Triggering
problem: A Jira automation rule does not execute when the expected event occurs.
symptoms: No audit-log execution appears.
Issues change without the expected automation action.
Only some projects or issue types may be affected.
causes: Branch or condition logic prevents execution.
quickFix: Open the automation audit log.
Confirm the rule is enabled.
Review the trigger event and conditions.
Check the rule scope and project association.
detailedFix: Test the trigger with a controlled issue.
Inspect each condition in order.
Verify the rule actor has the required permissions.
Check branch rules and smart-value assumptions.
Review recent changes to the project workflow.
diagnostics: Use audit logs to identify where execution stops.
Test conditions individually when possible.
Confirm the event actually fires for the relevant issue type.
prevention: Keep automation rules small, documented, tested, and owned by a team.

title: Azure 403 Forbidden Error
problem: An Azure request reaches the service but is rejected because access is not permitted.
symptoms: HTTP 403 response.
The resource is reachable but the operation is denied.
The issue can be resource-, identity-, or policy-specific.
quickFix: Identify the exact Azure resource and operation.
Confirm the identity making the request.
Check role assignments and applicable resource policies.
Review network restrictions if relevant.
detailedFix: Verify subscription and resource-group context.
Confirm the identity has the required least-privilege role.
Inspect resource-specific access settings.
Review Azure Policy or deny assignments when applicable.
Retest with a safe, read-only operation.
diagnostics: Record the request ID and timestamp.
Compare access using an approved test identity.
Check whether other users or workloads are affected.
prevention: Use least privilege, documented role ownership, and policy-aware deployment reviews.

title: Azure 401 Unauthorized Error
problem: An Azure API or service endpoint does not accept the supplied authentication credentials.
symptoms: HTTP 401 response.
Token or credential may be expired, invalid, or issued for the wrong audience.
quickFix: Confirm the endpoint and tenant.
Acquire a fresh credential using the approved flow.
Check that the token audience matches the service.
Avoid copying secrets into tickets or chat.
detailedFix: Inspect token metadata without exposing the token itself.
Verify application registration and permissions.
Confirm the requested scope/resource is correct.
Check service-specific authentication requirements.
diagnostics: Compare token issuer and audience metadata.
Check timestamps and expiration.
Review identity-provider logs when available.
prevention: Use managed identities or secure secret storage where supported and rotate credentials through approved processes.

title: Microsoft Teams Microphone Not Working
problem: Teams cannot capture microphone audio during a meeting or call.
symptoms: Other participants cannot hear the user.
Teams shows no microphone input.
Another application may still detect the microphone.
quickFix: Select the intended microphone in Teams settings.
Check operating-system microphone permissions.
Confirm the headset's hardware mute is off.
Test the microphone outside Teams.
detailedFix: Restart Teams after permission changes.
Check device drivers and OS audio settings.
Try a different approved device.
If managed, ask the administrator to check device or policy restrictions.
diagnostics: Determine whether the issue affects one device or multiple devices.
Check whether Teams receives any input level.
Test another meeting or supported audio application.
prevention: Keep Teams and device drivers current and document managed-device policies.

title: ServiceNow Workflow or Flow Is Not Running
problem: An expected ServiceNow workflow or flow does not execute.
symptoms: The triggering record changes but no flow action appears.
Execution history may show skipped or failed steps.
quickFix: Check execution details and flow status.
Confirm trigger conditions against the actual record.
Review failed actions and input values.
Verify the flow is active.
detailedFix: Use a controlled test record.
Inspect each condition and action.
Verify application scope and permissions.
Review system logs and execution details with appropriate administrator access.
diagnostics: Identify the exact record and timestamp.
Compare a working record with a failing record.
Check whether a recent update changed field values or conditions.
prevention: Use controlled deployments, versioned flows, and test cases for critical automation.

title: AWS AccessDenied Error
problem: An AWS API request is rejected because the effective permissions do not allow the requested action.
symptoms: AccessDenied response.
One role may fail while another succeeds.
The error can affect a specific resource or action.
quickFix: Identify the exact API action and resource.
Confirm which role or identity made the request.
Review effective permissions and explicit denies.
Avoid granting broad administrator access as a first fix.
detailedFix: Check identity policies and resource policies.
Inspect permissions boundaries and organization policies.
Verify the role trust relationship when assuming a role.
Retest with the minimum required permission.
diagnostics: Use request IDs and CloudTrail when available.
Compare a known-good identity with the failing role.
Check whether the failure is action-specific.
prevention: Use least privilege, policy reviews, and centralized identity governance.
